_meta.purpose: Domain glossary injected into the LLM system prompt so the model interprets dataset column names, units and TSO jargon correctly. Numbers always come from tool calls, never from this file.
_meta.system: IEEE-118 bus test system; regions r1/r2/r3; hourly snapshots for 2024

schema.bus_name: Bus (node) identifier, form 'bus_<n>'. A bus is a connection point in the grid.
schema.branch_name: Branch identifier 'branch_<from>_<to>_<parallel>'. A branch is a line or transformer.
schema.parallel: Index distinguishing parallel branches between the same two buses.
schema.gen_name: Generator identifier, form '<gen_type>_<n>' (e.g. solar_001, wind_003, chp).
schema.region: Region a bus belongs to (r1, r2, r3).
schema.in_service: True if the element is operating; False = out (maintenance/outage).
schema.is_slack: True if the bus is the slack/reference bus that balances the system.
schema.is_optimized: Whether the generator's output is set by the OPF optimisation stage.
schema.opt_category: OPF category of a generator (day_ahead / real_time / non_optimized).
schema.min_v_pu: Lower allowed bus voltage limit, in per unit (p.u.).
schema.max_v_pu: Upper allowed bus voltage limit, in per unit (p.u.).
schema.x_coordinate: Schematic x position of the bus (layout, not geographic).
schema.y_coordinate: Schematic y position of the bus (layout, not geographic).
schema.trafo_ratio_rel: Transformer turns ratio relative to the HV/LV voltage ratio (set only for transformers).
schema.max_i_ka: Thermal current limit of a branch in kiloamperes (kA). Loading is measured against this.
schema.p_mw: Active power in megawatts (MW). For a load = demand; for a generator = output.
schema.max_p_mw: Rated maximum active output of a generator (MW).
schema.min_p_mw: Rated minimum active output of a generator (MW).
schema.max_q_mvar: Max reactive output limit of a generator (MVAr), per its PQ diagram.
schema.min_q_mvar: Min reactive output limit of a generator (MVAr), per its PQ diagram.

results.loading_percent: How loaded a branch/transformer is vs its limit, in %. 100% = at the thermal limit. THE key risk metric.
results.vm_pu: Bus voltage magnitude in per unit (p.u.). 1.0 = nominal; must stay within min/max limits.
results.p_from_mw: Active power flowing into a branch at its 'from' end (MW).
results.pl_mw: Active power losses on a branch (MW).
results.res_bus: pandapower table of solved bus results (voltages, injections).
results.res_line: pandapower table of solved line results (flows, loading_percent).
results.res_trafo: pandapower table of solved transformer results.
results.ext_grid: External grid / slack connection that supplies or absorbs the balancing power.

domain.TSO: Transmission System Operator — operates the high-voltage grid (here: ČEPS). Keeps generation = consumption at all times.
domain.load flow: Power flow — calculation of how power, voltages and currents distribute across the grid for a given state.
domain.OPF: Optimal Power Flow — load flow that also optimises generator dispatch against costs/limits.
domain.AC-OPF: OPF using full AC physics (voltages, reactive power), more accurate than DC approximation.
domain.N-1: Security criterion: the grid must survive the outage of any single element without overloading the rest.
domain.N-1 secure: State where no single failure causes a limit violation.
domain.contingency: A hypothetical failure (line/transformer/generator trip) analysed for its impact.
domain.slack bus: Reference bus that makes up the difference between generation and load + losses.
domain.redispatch: Changing which generators produce (up here, down there) to relieve a congested element; usually has a cost.
domain.congestion: When a line/transformer would exceed its limit; flows must be rerouted or generation changed.
domain.curtailment: Deliberately reducing generator output (often renewables) when it cannot be absorbed or causes overload.
domain.demand response: Temporarily reducing/shifting consumer load to help balance or relieve the grid. Abbrev: DR.
domain.balancing: Keeping generation equal to consumption in real time to hold system frequency.
domain.day-ahead: Forecast/market for the next day. Abbrev: DA. The dataset's forecasts are day-ahead.
domain.intraday: Forecast/market within the same operating day, closer to real time. Abbrev: ID.
domain.reserve: Spare capacity (generators or storage) held ready to react to imbalances or failures.
domain.BESS: Battery Energy Storage System — can charge (load) or discharge (generation).
domain.CHP: Combined Heat and Power (cogeneration) plant; produces electricity and heat. Regulatable.
domain.prosumer: A consumer that also produces (e.g. household with rooftop solar).
domain.per unit: Normalised value relative to a base (e.g. voltage). 1.0 p.u. = nominal. Abbrev: p.u.
domain.binding constraint: The single most-loaded element that limits the whole system — the bottleneck.
domain.SCADA: Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition — the real-time monitoring/control system in the control room.
domain.WAMS: Wide Area Monitoring System — high-resolution synchronised grid measurements (PMU-based).
domain.dispatcher: Control-room operator who monitors the grid and decides operational actions.
domain.interconnector: A line/tie connecting two regions or countries; cross-region flows run over ties.

units.kV: Kilovolt — voltage level (here 138 kV and 345 kV).

czech.rozvodna: Substation (transformer station / node connecting voltage levels).
czech.teplárna: CHP / heating plant (combined heat and power).
